chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 409: Li Huowang Flushes Out the Zuowandao Emperor
chapter_meta_description: The Great Qi Emperor arrives—but Li Huowang instantly knows he's a Zuowandao. A fiery battle breaks out as Zhuge Yuan uses an almanac to rewrite reality.
og_title: The Emperor Is a Lie: Li Huowang vs. the Zuowandao
og_description: A burning, tooth-yanking showdown reveals the Zuowandao's tricks, but the final twist leaves Li Huowang clutching only a shadow puppet.
twitter_title: Li Huowang Sets Himself on Fire to Smoke Out the Zuowandao Emperor
twitter_description: The Great Qi Emperor is a Zuowandao impersonator. Li Huowang uses fire, teeth, and a reality-rewriting almanac to flush him out—only to find a burning puppet.

lore_anchors.definition: The ceremonial vehicle of a Chinese emperor; here it is depicted as an absurdly oversized, top-heavy wooden tower, creating a grotesque and oppressive presence.
A traditional Chinese calendar indicating auspicious and inauspicious days for various activities; Zhuge Yuan weaponizes it by imposing taboos that physically affect reality.
The imperial secret police of the Ming dynasty, renowned for their red robes and authority; in the Dao-Twisted World, they serve as the emperor’s enforcers.
A traditional Chinese folk performance using cut-out leather figures; the Zuowandao uses a burning shadow puppet as a decoy, highlighting their mastery of illusion.
A type of paper used for drawing talismans; in Daoist folk practice, it was believed to carry protective or empowering properties when inscribed with spells.
Traditional Chinese dominoes often used in folk gambling games; the Zuowandao weaponizes them as throwing knives in combat.
